findings.title: From defiance to a bounded campaign
findings.claim: The preceding threat to Adam's descendants gives the focus sequence a target: voice, gathered forces, participation in wealth and offspring, and promises operate as one campaign of recruitment. The following denial of authority bounds that campaign as an attempt to enlist people, not ownership of their will.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's sequence of destabilizing, vocal, mobilizing, partnership, and promise terms. The independent triggers are Iblis's refusal and threatened reach in 17:61-62, the followers and full recompense in 17:63, and the denied authority and guardianship in 17:65. Those contacts turn a list of methods into an operation aimed at the threatened lineage and bounded by the next ayah.
findings.reader_payoff: The methods become legible as a coordinated attempt to recruit and redirect human lives, with both its reach and its limit visible in the surrounding passage.
findings.containment: The focus still commands these methods and calls the promise delusion. The pericope does not say that every person follows or that Iblis has no influence at all. The proposed animal-roar branch is excluded because its registered collocation explicitly does not mean a human promise.

epistemic.reason: The supplied channel support and exact pericope occurrences ground the sequence and boundary; integrating them as one campaign remains an interpretive synthesis.

findings.title: From public pressure to intimate accommodation
findings.claim: The later pressure in 17:73-74 moves from attempted diversion and fabricated speech to intimacy and a near-leaning, with stabilization interrupting the sequence. Read beside the focus's voice, destabilization, and promises, this makes social accommodation a possible endpoint of recruitment.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the unsettling and promise terms. The independent triggers are the attempt to turn someone from what was revealed, the fabricated substitute and close friendship in 17:73, and the near-leaning and stabilization in 17:74. Their contact changes broad public influence into a possible route through altered speech and belonging, while the later stabilization marks a limit.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's voice and promise can be read as methods that reach toward a person's allegiance and relationships, not only as public propaganda.
findings.containment: The focus still names its own commands. Verses 17:73-74 may describe analogous human pressure rather than the adversary's direct operating chain; the finding preserves that alternative and does not identify the actors as one agent.

epistemic.reason: Every traced context coordinate and root matches the packet, but the reader identity is unbound and the connection between the two pressure sequences remains attributed.

findings.title: Destabilization with a spatial endpoint
findings.claim: The focus's destabilizing action returns in 17:76 immediately before removal from land and expulsion. This gives the earlier agitation a contextual spatial endpoint: a person may be unsettled until movement becomes displacement from place.
findings.mechanism: The focus occurrence of the repeated destabilizing root is the carrier. Its exact recurrence in 17:76 and the independent land and expulsion terms are the triggers. Their contact specifies a spatial form for the earlier destabilization and changes its possible endpoint from internal agitation alone to attempted removal from place.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how unsettling and expulsion connect in this pericope while the focus's psychological sense remains recoverable.
findings.containment: The focus still carries incitement or destabilization. The contextual verse describes opponents attempting to expel the addressed person and says their stay afterward would be brief; it does not claim that every destabilizing act ends in expulsion or permanent control.

epistemic.reason: The repeated root, land, and expulsion coordinates agree exactly with the packet, but the HFT reader identity is unbound and the focus-to-endpoint relation remains attributed.

findings.title: Partnership against exclusive allegiance
findings.claim: Under the external Fatiha lens, the focus command to participate in wealth and offspring meets the declaration that worship and aid belong to God alone. The root's theological association sense becomes audible as a boundary around the focus's social partnership.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus partnership verb with wealth and offspring as its named domains. The independent trigger is the Fatiha's explicit exclusive address in worship and seeking aid at 1:5. Their contact sets the adversarial partnership beside a declaration of exclusive allegiance and changes the material command into a locally bounded devotional contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The partnership command can be heard as touching allegiance as well as possessions and lineage, because the external declaration states whom the community worships and asks for aid.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay. The focus names participation in wealth and offspring; it does not say that anyone worships Satan or directly assert idolatry. The Fatiha supplies a contrast that makes the related branch audible without replacing the focus's material sense.

epistemic.reason: The focus word and external declaration are directly supplied, but treating their relation as an activation of the theological partnership branch is an interpretive overlay rather than a claim stated by either ayah alone.
